items.title: Palworld CEO wants to bring the game to Switch 2 despite ongoing Nintendo lawsuit
Palworld developer “of course” wants the game on Switch 2 as its simply “a really amazing platform”
items.summary: Is Palworld coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Well, not yet, but developer PocketPair would like it to eventually.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Palworld developer “of course” wants the game on Switch 2 as its simply “a really amazing platform” Published:

PocketPair, the studio behind Palworld , would really like to bring its open-world monster-catching survival game Palworld to the Nintendo Switch 2 .

Still working on additional support for the game , alongside a new, in-development Animal Crossing-esque spin-off, PocketPair has brought Palworld to every console platform other than Nintendo.

While the original Nintendo Switch was a little too weak for the game, Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe explained in a discussion with VGC that a Switch 2 port makes sense. “Of course,” the developer responded when asked if they want to bring the game to the new handheld.

“First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry. It’s been an incredible platform,” he continued.

Mizobe then stressed that there needs to be the “opportunity” to bring the game to Nintendo Switch 2, which likely means sorting out the studio’s ongoing lawsuit with Nintendo. While not mentioning the lawsuit, Pocketpair personally ported Palworld to Xbox One, PS4, Xbox Series, and PS5, so there’s certainly no lack of internal opportunity.

“If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations,” Mizobe told the outlet.

PocketPair and Nintendo’s ongoing legal case over Pokemon-like game mechanics is still active, and it’s not known what will happen if PocketPair loses. However, for now, Palworld remains one of the most popular games on Steam and other consoles, and it would be a great fit on Nintendo Switch 2.

For now, PocketPair is preparing to release Palworld Version 1.1, a sizeable but not “massive” update that will continue to expand the open-world survival game. The update is currently scheduled to launch sometime in Winter 2026.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

items.title: Palworld studio still hopes to release the game on Switch 2 one day, despite being in a legal battle with Nintendo
items.summary: The developer of viral hit Palworld still wants to bring the game to Switch 2, despite ongoing legal battle with Nintendo.
items.content:
Image credit: Pocketpair News by Sherif Saed Senior Contributor Published on Oct. 28, 2026, 2:03 p.m. 1 comment Follow Palworld Prioritise us on Google Palworld , the survival crafting game featuring adorable animals seemingly inspired by Pokémon, has been embroiled in a legal battle with Nintendo over what the company alleges is patent infringement . But although the lawsuit is ongoing, Palworld developer Pocketpair still says it's keen to bring the game to Switch 2 .

Speaking to VGC , Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he "of course" wants to bring the game to Nintendo's console. "First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry. It's been an incredible platform.

"If there's ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we'd love to have those conversations."

This stance isn't particularly surprising; Mizobe previously said it would be difficult to bring Palworld to the original Switch given how demanding the game is, but that could change if Switch 2 - the specs of which had yet to be revealed - has hardware capable enough to run the game. One year later, Pocketpair communications director John Buckley told IGN that a Switch 2 port was worth considering, assuming the console could handle the game.

Still, technical capabilities aside, we're not likely to see Palworld on Switch 2 until the lawsuit between Pocketpair and Nintendo is resolved. We're scheduled to hear an update on it soon, as the Tokyo District Court is set to issue a preliminary view on 9th November.

Palworld has sold over 30 million copies since its release in 2024, with July's 1.0 update attracting almost 1 million concurrent players on Steam .

items.title: Pocketpair Would Love to Release Palworld on Nintendo Switch 2, Despite Pokémon Legal Battle
items.summary: The legal battle between Nintendo and Pocketpair is ongoing, but the Palworld developer hasn’t ruled out a Switch 2 version of its creature collecting survival game.
items.content:
The legal battle between Nintendo and Pocketpair is ongoing, but the Palworld developer hasn’t ruled out a Switch 2 version of its creature collecting survival game.

Nintendo and The Pokémon Company are currently embroiled in ongoing litigation with Pocketpair in Japan, with patents that revolve around how Pokémon games work at the heart of the lawsuit. IP experts have indicated that Nintendo may only receive a $30,000 payout if it wins, but it's looking increasingly likely that Nintendo will lose.

Skirting around the elephant in the room in an interview with VGC , Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he’d love to get Palworld on Switch 2. “Of course,” Mizobe replied when asked if the studio had Switch 2 ambitions. “First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry.

“It’s been an incredible platform. If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations.”

Of course, the current legal dispute would have to play out before those conversations can happen, and that’s assuming there’s no bad blood once legal proceedings are done and dusted.

Nintendo filed a patent infringement lawsuit in September 2024, but the complaint was modified in November 2025 after Palworld updates changed some of the most egregious of the Pokemon-inspired game mechanics. One such mechanic was the ability to throw a sphere to summon a creature, which was removed in Early Access patch v0.3.11.

Now when you summon a Pal, it simply spawns directly beside your character while you hold out the sphere. This change to avoid stepping on Nintendo’s patent removed some of the tactical options the player had, since they were no longer able to summon a Pal to a specific spot to draw aggro or hit an enemy from a different angle.

The scope of the lawsuit is reduced, but Pocketpair versus Nintendo and The Pokémon Company remains an active case within the Tokyo District Court. A preliminary view — which is a first-impression assessment of a subject before all the facts are known or a final decision is made — is planned for November 9 this year.

Palworld hit its 1.0 release in July , netting close to 1 million concurrent players on Steam. In total, Palworld has reached over 40 million players .

items.title: Pocketpair would ‘love to have conversations’ to bring Palworld to Switch 2, CEO says
items.summary: Nintendo’s lawsuit surrounding the game is ongoing, but Pocketpair would like to bring Palworld to Switch 2…
items.content:
Nintendo’s lawsuit surrounding the game is ongoing, but Pocketpair would like to bring Palworld to Switch 2

Video Game News 27th Oct 2026 / 6:07 pm Posted by Chris Scullion The CEO of Pocketpair says he would love to see Palworld come to Nintendo Switch 2 in the future.

Back in June 2024, before the game’s release, Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he thought a Switch port would be unlikely due to the console’s technical capabilities.

This was seconded in an IGN interview with Pocketpair communications director John Buckley in March 2025, who said Palworld [113 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/palworld/ >Palworld is “a beefy game” that wouldn’t be possible on Nintendo Switch [6,286 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/switch/ >Switch , but that a Nintendo Switch 2 [1,637 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/nintendo-switch-2/ >Switch 2 port was “100% worth considering” if the specs (which weren’t known yet) were powerful enough.

Now, in a new interview with VGC , Mizobe was asked whether a Switch 2 port of Palworld was being considered as a real possibility, now that the specs are known to be capable enough to handle many of the current-gen games seen on other platforms.

“Of course,” Mizobe told us. “First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry. It’s been an incredible platform.

“If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations.”

items.content:
"We think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform," says Pocketpair's Takuro Mizobe

Pokemon and Nintendo filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Pocketpair over two years ago now, but even last year, prior to the Switch 2's launch, Pocketpair communications lead and publishing manager John "Bucky" Buckley said that porting Palworld to the platform was "100% worth considering" as long as the console was "beefy enough" to handle it.

And now, speaking in a new interview with VGC , Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says "of course" he still sees this idea as a real possibility. "First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry," he begins.

"It's been an incredible platform. If there's ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we'd love to have those conversations."

He's clearly not just saying that, either. After all, Pocketpair launched another of its games, the roguelike tower defense and card game title Overdungeon, on Switch at the start of last year, so the lawsuit isn't making it avoid Nintendo's platforms entirely.

New Nintendo Switch 2 games for 2026 and beyond Pocketpair lead says "TemTem are not our rivals" as it gets its own Palworld-like survival game Pocketpair lead thought if Palworld 1.0 hit 200k players, "that'd be party time" – it passed 900k Of course, the situation may be a tad more complicated when it comes to the idea of porting the very game at the center of the ongoing lawsuit, but Pocketpair and its boss at the very least aren't personally opposed, despite the circumstances. Perhaps when the lawsuit has been resolved – one way or another – we could finally see Palworld on the platform. After all, it's certainly "beefy" enough to support the likes of Cyberpunk 2077, the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy, and Elden Ring.

Palworld Side By Side is update 1.1 in a fancy hat, Pocketpair dev clarifies, not a new game or a "massive update."

items.title: Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld’s success
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio won’t let Palworld’s success dictate what comes next…
items.content:
Interview Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld’s success Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio won’t let Palworld’s success dictate what comes next

There’s an openness to Palworld developer Pocketpair that feels unusual in the games industry.

Its office in Gotanda, an up-and-coming entertainment district in Tokyo, is almost entirely open plan. From the CEO’s desk to the kitchen vending machines, there are no dividing walls, and the developer seems unconcerned with maintaining the air of secrecy that surrounds so many Japanese studios – even with a news journalist strolling around.

On social media, it has one of the most active community managers in the business, and visitors are often welcomed to drop by, stroll through its banks of developer desks, and have a go on the Palworld [113 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/palworld/ >Palworld -branded UFO catcher. It’s a far cry from other famous Japanese studios, which have been known to limit visits to closed meeting rooms and, sometimes, deny requests to use the bathroom.

Its approachability is particularly striking for a developer whose breakout success brought it a level of scrutiny that few independent studios experience. Palworld was barely out of the gate when its creature designs and eclectic combination of familiar mechanics attracted accusations of being derivative.

And then, of course, there was the Japanese lawsuit brought by The Pokémon Company , which alleges patent infringement, separate from the criticism that some of its creature designs bear conspicuous similarities to existing Pokémon video games [1,333 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/pokemon/ >Pokémon (with some later redesigned ).

At VGC, we extensively covered the controversy around Palworld in its early days and, more recently, published a 3/5 review of its 1.0 update . In my experience, other studios might have hunkered down, but it’s admirable that none of this changed Pocketpair’s willingness to talk.

Rather than dismissing our coverage, Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe [76 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/people/takuro-mizobe/ >Takuro Mizobe was keen to hear my take on why Palworld, a game that has clearly resonated hugely with players, so far has a critical consensus that doesn’t quite match the enthusiasm of players. The only off-limits topic was that Nintendo [6,915 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/ >Nintendo lawsuit, which Pocketpair said they couldn’t legally comment on.

Mizobe attributes Pocketpair’s openness to its unusual origins. Founded in 2015, the company grew out of his experience in web and technology businesses, rather than the traditional Japanese games industry.

“When I think about it, perhaps the Japanese games industry is a little more closed,” he told VGC. “But I don’t think that’s because companies are trying to hide anything or because they don’t want to be transparent.

“Historically, Japanese companies have placed a lot of importance on protecting their employees, maintaining security, and protecting information. Without going too deeply into the history of Japanese business, there have been a lot of hard lessons learned over the years.

“But Pocketpair didn’t really start in that traditional way. We started as a group of friends coming from web culture, and we’ve always had a very open-source kind of culture. Very early on, we set up a Discord server for our players, and we’ve always had this very open style of communication with our community.”

That culture has survived a transformation few could have predicted when Mizobe formed the company in 2015 with fellow university students. Pocketpair’s first game, card-action title Overdungeon, established its formula of combining eclectic genres together. Its next game, the Zelda- and Minecraft [376 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/minecraft/ >Minecraft -inspired Craftopia, gave Pocketpair its first big hit, selling over one million copies.

But nothing could prepare it for the near-overnight success of Palworld’s early access version, which launched for Xbox [11,892 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/xbox/ >Xbox and PC [13,152 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/pc/ >PC in January 2024 and amassed 25 million players in a single month (it now has more than 40m, according to the studio).

items.title: Palworld's First Official Toy Collection Is Here, Complete With Mystery Eggs and Adorable Pals
items.summary: Collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs.
items.content:
It's a good time to be a Palworld obsessive. The game recently teased its next update, Palworld: Side by Side , coming this winter, and now collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs. It's available now on Amazon .

Decorate your desk with the frankly adorable Chillet, take everyone's favorite oversized electric menace Grizzbolt out and about, and keep the perpetually vacant-looking Relaxasaurus in your pocket to remind you not to scream at your boss.

There are four different products in the collection, starting with a range of 4-inch articulated figures featuring Foxparks, Relaxasaurus, Grizzbolt, and Lifmunk. Each comes with its own Battle FX accessory, so you can make them fight without having to worry about a raid on your base.

For those who prefer their Pals a little smaller, because it's not the size of the Pal that matters but what you do with it that counts, there's also a 3-inch collector set featuring Chillet, Grizzbolt, and Relaxasaurus ( see at Amazon ).

And because apparently collecting Pals in the game wasn't enough, there are two different mystery collections to hunt down. The Cheebee Micro Blind Mystery Pal Egg 12-Pack includes a dozen 1.5-inch mystery figures, while the Blind Egg Incubator Reveal 8-Pack offers eight miniature Pals to hatch and collect.

As always, the blind-box format means there's no guarantee you'll get the Pal you're after, so happy hunting to all the completionists out there. At least these ones won't require you to craft hundreds of Pal Spheres.

The collection is available to pre-order now on Amazon .

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

could use some skills through walls or in other situations where they could not see the player ▼Items and Shops ・Fixed an issue where selling multiple items at a shop could calculate the sale amount incorrectly ・Fixed an issue where item counts could fail to update correctly under certain conditions when moving items ・Fixed an issue where Radiant Gems dropped by wild Pals in the World Tree area could have mismatched or overly biased elements ▼Bases and Building ・Fixed an issue where color picking and editing could fail to work correctly in Paint Mode ・Fixed an issue where diagonally connecting corner roofs could result in unnatural placement ・Fixed an issue where stairs placed on the side of a corner roof could face an unnatural direction ・Fixed an issue where Worker Pal assignments might not be correctly reflected in Base Facilities ・Fixed an issue where chest access permissions were not correctly applied to material reference and consumption when crafting at a base ・Fixed an issue where the work speed multiplier would not be correctly applied after resuming the game with the Ancient Material Synthesizer ▼UI, Display, and Text ・Fixed an issue on the World Select screen where the displayed multiplayer setting could differ from the actual setting ・Fixed an issue where some key icons could appear as Xbox controller icons when using a PS5 controller on PC ・Fixed an issue where operating the chat UI with a gamepad could unintentionally close chat ・Fixed an issue where hold input did not work correctly for Pal Soul enhancement ・Fixed an issue where the HUD ammo count could remain at 0 after reloading a regular weapon ▼Field and Map ・If the map around an unlocked Watchtower remains unexplored, accessing the same Watchtower again will now unlock the map ・Fixed an issue where temperature might not be applied correctly on Bicornis Islet ・Fixed an issue where items dropped from gathering objects in the field could become buried in the ground ▼Fishing ・Fixed an issue where the fishing reward display could show the same type of item in multiple slots ▼Sound ・Fixed an issue where the Attack Chopper’s propeller sound could continue playing ・Fixed an issue where BGM could unintentionally play on the loading screen after the World Tree boss battle ・Fixed an issue where Base Raid BGM or battle BGM could unintentionally play during cutscenes ▼Mods ・Fixed an issue on Steam where Mod files could not be deleted correctly ▼Other Minor Bug Fixes▼ ・Fixed translations for guild join, leave, login, and logout notifications ・Fixed an issue where a marker could remain after completing Main Mission “Awakening” ・Fixed an issue where the mission marker was not displayed for Sub Mission “Collecting Pure Quartz” ・Fixed the marker position for No. 1 Wildlife Sanctuary in Zoe’s sub-mission ・Fixed an issue where mission NPCs could remain standing upright after death ・Fixed an issue where NPC animations could switch unnaturally during the ending ・Fixed an issue where Panthalus’s body collision did not match its appearance ・Fixed an issue where “Mercy Hit” could be displayed even when its conditions were not met ・Fixed an issue where Paladius’s Partner Skill could summon an Alpha Necromus from the player’s party at normal size ・Fixed an issue where the collision of Logging Site II could remain during building preview ・Fixed a Palbox UI misalignment that could occur when Base Pal slots were displayed in four rows ・Fixed an issue where building name text could overlap with the power icon ・Fixed the direction of the arrow indicating the front side of the Clinic ・Fixed an issue where the guild master transfer dialog text would not be displayed correctly based on the situation ・Fixed an issue where an unnecessary key guide could appear on the Pal Effigies enhancement screen ・Fixed the turning guide icon for the Wing Pack ・Fixed an issue where a black square could appear at the edge of the map filter UI ・Fixed an issue where the Field Boss icon for Prixter Lux was not displayed correctly ・Fixed an issue where unintended Pals could be caught at some fishing spots in volcanic areas ・Fixed an issue on Dedicated Servers where attacking a sleeping Galeclaw could cause it to fall through the ground ・Fixed an issue where unintended BGM would play when starting dialogue with a Black Marketeer ＝＝＝ Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.

items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released!

＝＝＝

\

▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon.

・Changed the technology unlock level of the Aquatic Construction Kit from Level 66 to Level 23, changed its Ancient Technology Point requirement from 4 to 1, and adjusted the required materials and work amount.

・Extended the duration of World Tree Holy Water.

・Reduced the weight of World Tree Holy Water from 1 to 0.1.

・Added World Tree Holy Water to the rewards for World Tree expeditions, World Tree fishing, and the Large Fishing Pond.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

・Fixed an issue where items could duplicate when performing certain actions.

・Fixed an issue where, when Katress's Partner Skill activated, switching spheres while riding could allow the player to obtain a different type of sphere.

・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Holy Water effect did not display correctly on the Pal being ridden when using World Tree Holy Water while riding.

・Fixed an issue where, after the World Tree Holy Water effect ended, riding a Pal would cause the World Tree Holy Water aura to reappear and not disappear when approaching trees in The World Tree area.

・Fixed an issue where an unintended reward was set for the desert expedition.

・Fixed an issue where the Dark Skill Fruit: Psycho Gravity did not appear on the item search screen.

・Fixed a bug where the firing interval was not set for sphere launchers

▼UI, Display, and Text

・Fixed an issue where resolution settings would not apply correctly in fullscreen mode.

・Fixed an issue where, after switching window mode with F11 / Alt+Enter, the game could unintentionally return to fullscreen mode after loading.

・Fixed an issue where, if certain effects were on screen while aiming, the entire screen could become blurred.

▼Sound

・Fixed an issue where the water sound effect could fail to play at Teafant Spring.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where the BGM for Attack Choppers triggered by other players could play even from far away.

・Adjusted the BGM playback range for Attack Choppers so that it plays correctly for players who are Wanted.

・Fixed an issue where unintended footstep sounds could play when walking on furniture or facilities.

▼Controls

・Fixed an issue where, after changing the key assignment for ""Attack that enemy!"" in Controls, selecting ""Restore to Default"" would not restore the default setting.

・Fixed an issue where settings could be applied unintentionally when interacting with the change confirmation dialog and duplicate key warning in Controls.

▼Map and Exploration

・Fixed an issue where a beach-like display could remain on the water surface after Fast Traveling to an offshore base.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.
